title: Video-Assisted Patient Education in Radiation Therapy for Prostate Cancer
summary:
Previous studies from various fields of medicine show that when patients also watch an educational video, they understand the content better and are more satisfied. They are also more likely to follow the preparation instructions for radiation therapy. For doctors, a video usually saves time. This can help reduce staff shortages and costs. To date, there have been few studies on this topic in the field of radiation therapy.
In this study, we aim to determine whether an informational video benefits patients with prostate cancer prior to radiation therapy.

interventions.name: Study Arm A: Conventional radiation therapy patient education
Study Arm B: Video-assisted radiation therapy patient education

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Histologically confirmed diagnosis of prostate cancer
- Indication for definitive radiation therapy
- ECOG performance status 0–2
- Age ≥ 18 years
- Willingness to complete questionnaires
- Sufficient written and spoken German language skills to understand the content of the videos and questionnaires
- Ability to provide informed consent.
- Submission of a written informed consent form
Exclusion criteria:
- Previous radiation therapy
- Lack of capacity to give consent
